relationships.subject: TNF-alpha
relationships.evidence_quote: Consistently, WB analysis revealed a marked increase in Nav1.7 protein expression following TNF-α stimulation (P < 0.001, 95.00% CI = 7.89–8.16) (Fig. 2C).

relationships.subject: BRD4
relationships.evidence_quote: Consistently, WB analysis revealed that Nav1.7 protein levels were significantly elevated following TNF-α stimulation (P < 0.001, 95.00% CI = −0.8013 to −0.5987) and were substantially suppressed by BRD4 silencing (P < 0.001, 95.00% CI = 1.339–1.541) (Fig. 3C).

relationships.subject: BRD4
relationships.evidence_quote: Consistently, WB analysis showed that MMP13 protein expression was markedly increased in the TNF-α group compared with the Ctrl group (P < 0.001, 95.00% CI = −1.538 to −1.342), and significantly suppressed by BRD4 knockdown (P < 0.001, 95.00% CI = 2.039–2.235) (Supplementary Fig. 3I).

relationships.subject: Nav1.7
relationships.evidence_quote: These findings indicate that the loss of Nav1.7 in chondrocytes exerts a protective effect by alleviating both structural pathology and pain perception in OA.

relationships.subject: ProTx II
relationships.evidence_quote: Both treatments significantly reduced sodium current amplitudes relative to the TNF-α group (Fig. 2I).

key_findings: BRD4 enhances Scn9a/Nav1.7 transcription in chondrocytes, driving mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation and catabolism in osteoarthritis.
Chondrocyte-specific Nav1.7 knockout reduces cartilage degeneration and pain behaviors in DMM and MIA models; a cartilage-targeted BRD4 PROTAC hydrogel is therapeutic.
